To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the stiffness of the microenvironment is a critical determinant of neural stem cell fate, and that a synthetic, interpenetrating network hydrogel system can be used to study this phenomenon.

we developed a new synthetic hydrogel system that allows independent control over biochemical signals, cell adhesion, and substrate moduli, and that we used this system to demonstrate that the mechanical properties of the aNSC microenviroment can be tuned to direct the self renewal and neuronal differentiation of aNSC.

the stiffness of the substrate and the biochemical cues presented by the substrate can independently regulate the self renewal, differentiation, and proliferation of aNSCs, and that aNSC self renewal, differentiation and proliferation are regulated by the substrate's stiffness and biochemical cues presented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a synthetic, interpenetrating network hydrogel system to control stem cell self renewal, differentiation, and migration.
the development of synthetic biomaterials for neural tissue engineering.
the development of synthetic hydrogel systems for the study of stem cell self renewal, proliferation, and differentiation, and the effects of soluble and interfacial cues on these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanical properties of an a NSC microenvironment can direct the self renewal and neuronal and glial differentiation of a NSCs.

the mechanical properties of the microenvironment can direct stem cell behavior, and that the effects of soluble cues and adhesion ligand density can be modulated by the mechanical properties of an interfacial culture system.
the vmIPN system is an effective platform to study the effects of material stiffness and ligand presentation on stem cell self renewal, differentiation and cell spreading.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanical environment can be used to control stem cell self renewal, differentiation and proliferation.
aNSC behavior can be regulated by the presentation of soluble factors, adhesive ligands, and substrate moduli.
the mechanical properties of the microenvironment regulate stem cell function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have developed a novel synthetic interfacial hydrogels that can be used to independently control biochemical and mechanical cues to regulate stem cell function.

the material stiffness of the culture substrate can be used to direct the fate of aNSCs, and the vmIPN culture system provides a means to independently tune material stiffness and biochemical signals to investigate the combined effect of these parameters on stem cell behavior.
the mechanical properties of the extracellular environment can be tuned to modulate the behavior of neural stem cells.
